<h>Lectio 1</h>
De Epístola beáti Iacóbi Apóstoli
<r>Ias 3:1-3</r>
<n>1</n> Nolíte plures magístri fíeri fratres mei, sciéntes quóniam maius iudícium súmitis.
<n>2</n> In multis enim offéndimus omnes. Si quis in verbo non offéndit, hic perféctus est vir: potest étiam freno circumdúcere totum corpus.
<n>3</n> Si autem equis frena in ora míttimus ad consentiéndum nobis, et omne corpus illórum circumférimus.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> In toto corde meo, allelúia, exquisívi te, allelúia:
* Ne repéllas me a mandátis tuis, allelúia, allelúia.
<r>℣.</r> Benedíctus es tu, Dómine, doce me iustificatiónes tuas.
<r>℟.</r> Ne repéllas me a mandátis tuis, allelúia, allelúia.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the letter of St. James the Apostle
<r>Jas 3:1-3</r>
<n>1</n> Be ye not many masters, my brethren, knowing that you receive the greater judgment.
<n>2</n> For in many things we all offend. If any man offend not in word, the same is a perfect man. He is able also with a bridle to lead about the whole body.
<n>3</n> For if we put bits into the mouths of horses, that they may obey us, and we turn about their whole body.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> With my whole heart, alleluia, have I sought thee, alleluia.
* O let me not wander from thy commandments, alleluia, alleluia.
<r>℣.</r> Blessed art Thou, O Lord; teach me thy statutes.
<r>℟.</r> O let me not wander from thy commandments, alleluia, alleluia.

<n>8</n> Linguam autem nullus hóminum domáre potest: inquiétum malum, plena venéno mortífero.

b.2ed871b18c:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>Q</c>uarto Kaléndas Maii Luna vicésima secúnda. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>S</h>ancti Pauli a Cruce, Presbýteri et Confessóris; qui Congregatiónis a Cruce et Passióne Dómini nostri Iesu Christi nuncupátæ Institútor fuit, atque in Dómino obdormívit quintodécimo Kaléndas Novémbris.
<h>R</h>avénnæ natális sancti Vitális Mártyris, viri sanctæ Valériæ ac patris sanctórum Gervásii et Protásii; qui, cum beáti Ursicíni corpus sublátum débita honestáte sepelísset, tentus est a Paulíno Consulári, et, post equúlei torménta, iussus depóni in profúndam fóveam, et terra ac lapídibus óbrui; talíque martýrio migrávit ad Christum.
<h>A</h>tínæ, in Campánia, sancti Marci, qui, a beáto Petro Apóstolo Epíscopus ordinátus, Æquícolis primus Evangélium prædicávit, et in persecutióne Domitiáni, sub Máximo Prǽside, martýrii corónam accépit.
<h>P</h>rusæ, in Bithýnia, sanctórum Mártyrum Patrícii Epíscopi, Acátii, Menándri et Polyǽni.
<h>E</h>ódem die sanctórum Mártyrum Aphrodísii, Caralíppi, Agápii et Eusébii.
<h>I</h>n Pannónia sancti Polliónis Mártyris, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre.
<h>M</h>edioláni sanctæ Valériæ Mártyris, uxóris sancti Vitális ac matris sanctórum Gervásii et Protásii.
<h>A</h>lexandríæ pássio sanctæ Theodóræ, Vírginis et Mártyris. Hæc, idólis sacrificáre contémnens, in lupánar est trádita, sed repénte quidam ex frátribus, nómine Dídymus, miro Dei favóre, commutátis véstibus, illam erípuit; qui póstea, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, sub Eustrátio Prǽside, simul cum eádem Vírgine percússus, simul coronátus est.
<h>T</h>uriasóne, in Hispánia Tarraconénsi, sancti Prudéntii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>C</h>orfínii, in Pelígnis, sancti Pámphili, Valvénsis Epíscopi, caritáte in páuperes et virtúte miraculórum illústris; cuius corpus Sulmóne cónditum est.
<h>I</h>n pago sancti Lauréntii ad Séparim, diœcésis Lucionénsis, sancti Ludovíci Maríæ Grignion a Montfort, Confessóris, Fundatóris Missionariórum Societátis Maríæ et Filiárum a Sapiéntia, apostólicæ vitæ forma, prædicatióne et devotióne mariáli insígnis, quem Pius Papa Duodécimus Sanctórum catálogo adscrípsit.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.01e6024771:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>A</c>pril 28th 2027, the 22nd day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>W</h>e keep the feast of the holy Confessor Paul of the Cross, founder of the congregation
<h>c</h>alled that of the Cross and Passion of our Lord Jesus Christ, and of whom mention is made upon the 18th day of October, upon the which day, [in the year 1775,] he fell asleep in the Lord.
<h>A</h>t Ravenna, the holy martyr Vitalis, father of holy Gervase and Protase. He had removed the body of blessed Ursicinus and buried it with due respect for the which cause he was arrested by Paulinus the consular, and when they had racked him, they cast him into a deep pit and buried him alive under earth and stones, and with that testimony he passed away to be with Christ, [in the year 171.]
<h>A</h>t Atino, holy Mark, who was ordained Bishop of that see by the blessed Apostle Peter, and was the first that preached the Gospel to the Equicoli, [inhabitants of the Campania round Rome.] He received the crown of martyrdom under the President Maximus, in the persecution under the Emperor Domitian.
<h>A</h>t Brusa, in Bithynia, the holy martyr Patrick, Bishop of [that see,] Acatius, Menander, and Polyaenus, [third century.]
<h>U</h>pon the same day, the holy martyrs Aphrodisius, [first Bishop of Beziers,] Caralippus, Agapius, and Eusebius, [in the year 65.]
<h>I</h>n Hungary, under the Emperor Diocletian, the holy martyr Pollio. [He was a Reader in the church of Cibales, in the country of Valentinian. Cibales was between the rivers Save and Drave, and is now in ruins. St Pollio suffered on the same day, though at a distance of some years, as his Bishop Eusebius.]
<h>A</h>t Milan, the holy martyr Valeria, wife of holy Vitalis.
<h>A</h>t Alexandria, the holy Virgin Theodora. She would not sacrifice to idols and was sent to a brothel; but one of the brethren, named Didymus, by the favour of God changed clothes with her, and so delivered her thence. Later on, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, they were beheaded together under Eustratius the President, and so were crowned together.
<h>A</h>t Tarazona, in Spain, the holy Confessor Prudentius, Bishop [of that see, before the year 846.]
<h>A</h>t Pentina, in the Abruzzi, [in the seventh century,] holy Pamphilus, Bishop of Valva, famous for his charity to the poor and gift of miracles. He is buried at Sulmona.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
